ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision), effective 1 January 2025; Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 of 2024), effective 1 November 2024; Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; Regulation on the Administration of Enterprise Name Registration and SAMR market-entry registration rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign JV partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry in the foreign partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive paths: (A) if the origin state is party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, notarize if required, then obtain an apostille from the designated competent authority, and never pursue consular legalization; (B) if the origin state is not a member, execute notarization, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication in the origin country, then consular legalization by the PRC Embassy/Consulate, and never apply an apostille. After either path, attach a certified Chinese translation and notarize the translation before filing with SAMR.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Corporate Status of the foreign JV partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or analogous competent authority in the foreign partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive paths: (A) Hague Apostille path for Apostille Convention states - notarize if required, then apostille by competent authority, with no consular step; (B) Consular Legalization path for non-member states - origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization followed by legalization by the PRC Embassy/Consulate, with no apostille step. In both paths the authenticated document must be translated into Chinese by a certified translator and the translation notarized in China before submission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture and appointment of the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign JV partner's board of directors, notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track (if member): notarization + apostille by the origin competent authority; use no consular legalization. Consular track (if non-member): notarization + origin country Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication + PRC consular legalization; use no apostille. The two tracks are exclusive alternatives and must never be chained sequentially. Add certified Chinese translation and notarization in China.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or constitutional instruments of the foreign JV partner (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or notary public in the foreign partner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel paths: (A) Apostille Convention member: certify/notarize the copy and affix apostille through the designated competent authority; no consular legalization. (B) Non-member: certify/notarize, authenticate at the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then apply to the PRC Embassy/Consulate for consular legalization; no apostille. Never combine apostille with consular legalization. Provide Mandarin translation by licensed translator and PRC notarization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and account conduct statement for the foreign JV partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of the foreign JV partner, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive authentication tracks only: (A) Apostille: officer's signature notarized, then apostille by the state competent authority; no consular legalization. (B) Consular: officer's signature notarized, then origin Foreign Ministry legalization, then PRC Embassy/Consulate legalization; no apostille. Thereafter, the bank letter is translated into Chinese and the translation notarized before it is accepted by SAMR or a Chinese bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports and UBO identification documents for all directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign partner's jurisdiction or the issuing passport/ID authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Use either the Hague Apostille path (notarization + apostille by competent authority for Apostille Convention states, without consular legalization) or the Consular Legalization path (notarization + origin Foreign Ministry legalization + PRC consular legalization for non-member states, without apostille). The two authentication frameworks are parallel and mutually exclusive; never apply both sequentially. Provide certified Chinese translations and PRC notarization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, senior managers, and foreign JV partners must be screened continuously against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the U.S. OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the domestic lists maintained by the PBOC and the Ministry of Public Security. Politically exposed persons, regardless of category (domestic PEP, foreign PEP, or international-organization PEP), trigger mandatory enhanced due diligence under PBOC Order [2016] No. 3 and the 2024 PBOC/SAMR beneficial-owner order, requiring senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring for at least 12 months after any customer relationship ends. Any sanctions or negative-news hit must be escalated to the AML compliance officer, reported to the China Counter-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center, and resolved through refusal or filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report before any capital contribution or share transfer is completed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Declaration System / National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) online name pre-screening portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in simplified Chinese characters. The four-tier naming convention is: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry/organizational characterization + company form. The English name is auxiliary and must be a faithful transliteration or translation of the approved Chinese name. A foreign investor's corporate or personal name must be transliterated using standard Mandarin pinyin unless a pre-approved recognized Chinese name already exists. Latin letters and Arabic numerals are allowed only where expressly permitted by SAMR for special zones or technology enterprises and must not create ambiguity with prohibited or sensitive words.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain a written statement of reasons from the SAMR registration office. Within 15 days of receipt, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration application with the next-higher SAMR, enclosing the rejection notice, the proposed rectified name, a legalization-bearing power of attorney, and the joint venture contract draft. The reviewing authority must decide within 60 days, extendable to 75 days in complex cross-border cases. If the reconsideration is dismissed or denied, an administrative lawsuit may be filed in the competent primary people's court within 15 days of service of the reconsideration decision. During the reservation window, a rejected name may immediately be resubmitted after removing the offending elements only if the re-submission does not exceed the 30-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial-mailbox-only registered address is not permissible for this Sino-Foreign Equity Joint

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), relevant provisions on establishment, corporate governance, registered capital, legal representative, directors, supervisors, and registration, including Articles governing incorporation, the articles of association, share subscription, and statutory officers; supplemented by the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), in particular national treatment, foreign investment information reporting, and the Foreign Investment Negative List; and the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (2021), including the provisions on establishment registration and unified social credit codes.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) Enterprise Registration Department at the district or county level of the company's proposed registered office, exercising delegated registration authority under the Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Company (SAMR standard form), together with the executed Chinese Articles of Association and the required shareholder, director, supervisor, legal representative, and registered office attachment dossiers.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None for this business scope. A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture limited liability company engaging in stock photography marketplace and generative visual assets is not subject to a statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked capital account is required at incorporation. Under the 2023 Company Law, shareholders must subscribe the registered capital in writing and pay the subscribed contributions within five years from establishment, unless a shorter period is set in the Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_JV_LTD (SINO-FOREIGN EQUITY JOINT VENTURE LIMITED COMPANY). WHEREAS, the shareholders of the Company have executed the Articles of Association and the Company has received a business license from the competent Market Supervision Administration; WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is convened in accordance with the Articles of Association and the Company Law of the People's Republic of China; WHEREAS, all duly elected founding directors are present and constitute a quorum; AND WHEREAS, the founding shareholders have subscribed to the registered capital, proposed authorized bank signatories, selected a registered office, and nominated statutory officers; NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS HEREBY RESOLVES THAT: 1. The subscription, amount and timetable of the registered capital of the Company are ratified and confirmed. The registered capital is RMB [AMOUNT], to which the Chinese shareholder subscribes RMB [AMOUNT] and the foreign shareholder subscribes RMB [AMOUNT] in cash or lawful non-monetary property. The Chairperson is authorized to demand paid-in contributions in accordance with the Articles and to ensure that each contribution is deposited into the Company's basic deposit account. The Board acknowledges that for the Company's designated business scope of stock photography marketplace and generative visual assets, no minimum statutory paid-up capital is required. 2. The Board authorizes the opening and maintenance of all corporate bank accounts with licensed commercial banks, including a basic deposit account, a capital account for foreign-exchange investments, general deposit accounts and payment-rail accounts for cross-border payment services such as Stripe and PayPal. The Legal Representative and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly, are empowered, without further board action, to select, open, close, sign account mandates, operate, download statements, and bind the seals of the Company. 3. The registered office of the Company is adopted as the registered address at [ADDRESS], and the Board approves the lease agreement, the landlord's certificate of title, and any consent to registration. The Company Secretary shall ensure that the lease remains current and shall notify the registry of any relocation within the statutory period. 4. The Board appoints [NAME] as Chairperson of the Board and Legal Representative; [NAME] as General Manager; [NAME] as Chief Financial Officer; [NAME] as Supervisor; and [NAME] as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, with the powers and duties provided by the Articles of Association and applicable law. The Legal Representative is directed to complete all post-registration filings, including seal carving, tax registration, social insurance, foreign investment information reporting and any applicable licensing, and to deliver a written compliance report at the next subsequent meeting. UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name verification and negative-list screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) online name verification system; local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) business registration service window at the district level of the proposed registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the SAMR online name verification system or the local district market supervision bureau service window and file a one-shot name application for a Sino-foreign equity joint venture limited company. State the proposed Chinese name, registered office district, business scope, shareholder identities, and liability structure. The name must follow the statutory order: administrative division, trade name, industry characteristic, and company type, and must not be identical or deceptively similar to an already-registered name. Because the intended activities are not in the Foreign Investment Negative List, no preliminary government authorization needs to be obtained; however, the name application should include the full proposed business scope for photography stock media and AI visual assets to avoid later scope amendments.
required_dossiers: Applicant identity card or passport
Proposed company name list of at least three alternatives
Shareholder identification including Chinese business license or foreign passport and corporate certificate
Draft business scope in Chinese
Intended registered office administrative district
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identical or deceptively similar marks, submit a fresh alternative name list within the same portal. If an administrative error is suspected, request administrative reconsideration from the supervising SAMR office within sixty days or directly file a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authentication, translation and preparation of incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary office in the People's Republic of China for domestic attestation; apostille or consular legalization authority in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction; certified translation firm in the People's Republic of China; legal counsel for drafting corporate governance documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing, the foreign shareholder must deliver notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized corporate records from its home jurisdiction, including certificate of incorporation, corporate charter, board resolution authorizing investment, and good standing certificate issued within six months. All foreign documents must be translated into Chinese by a certified translation agency and the Chinese versions attested. The Chinese shareholder must provide an official copy of its business license and legal representative identification. The legal counsel shall prepare the Articles of Association in Chinese, containing the entire share subscription schedule, board composition, authorized capital, transfer restrictions, and officer powers, and shall obtain the landlord's property certificate and a leased-office location that is suitable for the registered office. All founding shareholders, directors, supervisors and the general manager shall sign or acknowledge the charter and consent forms.
required_dossiers: Apostilled or consular-legalized foreign shareholder incorporation certificate and good standing certificate issued within six months
Certified Chinese translation of all foreign corporate documents
Chinese shareholder's business license and legal representative identification copy
Executed Chinese Articles of Association
Lease agreement and landlord property certificate
Consent and identification forms for directors, supervisor, general manager and legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If authentication is rejected because the certificate is stale or lacks apostille or legalization, obtain a fresh certificate from the issuer or the competent apostille office. If a Chinese translation has omissions, have the certified translator correct and resubmit with the translator's seal and a translator-certified copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of establishment registration to the Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) Enterprise Registration Department at the district level; provincial government one-stop enterprise registration online portal coordinated with SAMR data systems.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation application through the local Market Supervision Administration enterprise-registration electronic system or in person at the district-level registration hall. The filing must include the standard Application for Establishment Registration of a Company, the executed Chinese Articles of Association, shareholder identity documents, notarized foreign documents, nominee director and supervisor identifications, consent letters, and the registered office lease plus property-certificate copy. The regulator performs a structural review of capital, governance, negative-list compliance and address; there is no administrative registration fee. Upon successful review, the registry issues a unified social credit code and a business license. After issuance, the Foreign Investment Information Report is filed separately under the Foreign Investment Law within the statutory deadline.
required_dossiers: Standard Application for Establishment Registration of a Company (SAMR form)
Approved name pre-registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Proof of registered office including lease and title certificate
Valid identity documents of shareholders and officers
Foreign shareholder corporate resolution authorizing incorporation
Negative-list self-declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction note, cure the deficiency within five working days and resubmit through the same tracking number. If the application is suspended for suspected negative-list or fraud issues, provide supplemental explanation and evidence; after a final refusal, apply for administrative reconsideration within sixty days or judicial review within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration official seal, tax, social insurance and bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving enterprises; local tax service hall of the State Taxation Administration; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Fund Management Center; licensed commercial banks for account opening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, arrange for carving of the company seal, financial seal, contract seal and legal representative seal at a Public Security Bureau licensed seal engraving enterprise, and file the seal specimen with the local police. Complete tax registration through the multi-license integration system, including obtainment of the taxpayer identification number, payroll withholding registration, and finance and accounting system filing, by visiting the local tax service hall or using the electronic tax bureau. Register the entity for social insurance and housing fund with the local human resources and social security bureau and housing fund management center. With the seal and license, open a RMB basic deposit account with a licensed commercial bank, and thereafter a general deposit account and foreign-exchange settlement account as needed.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Legal representative identification and company seal
Tax registration form generated by the electronic tax bureau
Social insurance registration form
Bank account opening application and board resolution
Seal specimen card from the Public Security Bureau licensed engraver
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is not synchronized automatically, apply manually in the local tax hall using the unified social credit code. If the bank declines the account opening due to incomplete lease or documentation, supplement the landlord certificate or choose another licensed bank; if the seal engraving is refused, obtain Public Security Bureau approval or use only a licensed engraving shop.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment information reporting, foreign exchange registration and digital platform filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the national foreign investment information reporting system or the market regulation data-sharing platform; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) local branch through the designated bank; provincial Communications Administration for any applicable internet content or data platform filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty working days of the issuance of the business license, submit the initial Foreign Investment Information Report to the Ministry of Commerce through the national foreign investment information reporting system or the market regulation data-sharing platform, stating the amount of foreign equity, ultimate beneficial owners, and planned paid-in schedule. If capital is injected from abroad, open a capital account with the designated bank and complete foreign-exchange registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange branch through the bank; provide the bank with a board resolution and the company seal. For the stock-media and AI digital platform, complete the non-physical data and telecommunication filing applicable to internet content or online platforms if the platform servers are hosted within China, and keep documentary evidence of the filing. No industrial or physical environmental license is triggered because the business is a pure digital and consulting operation.
required_dossiers: Business license with unified social credit code
Executed board resolution on officers and bank mandates
Foreign investor identity and ownership certificate
Foreign-exchange capital account opening and SAFE registration receipt
Signed initial Foreign Investment Information Report
Internet content or platform filing acceptance letter if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Foreign Investment Information Report is returned with validation flags, amend and resubmit within the statutory correction window to avoid penalties. If SAFE delays the foreign-exchange registration or capital account, request in writing a reason, provide the apostilled shareholder identity and source-of-funds statement, and escalate to the branch's supervisory desk; if a filing denial occurs for the digital platform, migrate servers to a compliant hosting arrangement or adjust the platform's content classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing authority is engaged for a pure digital and consulting stock-photo and AI visual-asset marketplace; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are conducted.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - pure digital and consulting stock-photo and AI visual-asset platform; no physical manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility exists; therefore no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or industrial occupational clearance is required. The registered office must nonetheless comply with ordinary commercial building fire safety and workplace safety rules under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online filing and tax registration through the unified National Electronic Tax Bureau, commonly called the Electronic Tax Bureau internet portal (chinatax.gov.cn/etax).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is first incorporated with the local State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The USCC is the sole statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and is also used for VAT, Enterprise Income Tax, customs, social insurance, and payroll tax purposes. Within 30 days after the business license issue date, the legal representative or authorized tax agent must complete tax registration through the Electronic Tax Bureau portal by submitting the business license, USCC, articles of association, registered office proof, legal representative identification, capital/bank account information, and intended accounting and tax-filing arrangements. The STA confirms the USCC as the TIN and opens the taxpayer master file, VAT general taxpayer profile, and tax return channels. A foreign non-resident entity without a PRC establishment or place of business does not ordinarily obtain a standalone PRC TIN; where the foreign enterprise is subject to withholding, the PRC payor withholds using the foreign entity's home-country tax reference, while a non-resident with a PRC permanent establishment or otherwise directly taxable in China must apply for non-resident tax registration through the same Electronic Tax Bureau gateway using its foreign TIN and, if applicable, the Chinese establishment USCC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Chinese-incorporated equity joint venture is a PRC resident limited liability enterprise taxed on its worldwide income; flow-through/pass-through status is not available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide US-style check-the-box elections or formal hybrid mismatch elections; tax treatment is determined by the Enterprise Income Tax Law, and hybrid arrangements are countered under the PRC General Anti-Avoidance Rule and special anti-avoidance rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: China Value-Added Tax (VAT); general services at 9% or 6% depending on classification, goods at 13%, and certain export/offshore supplies at 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All taxpayers must complete USCC/tax registration before commencing taxable activity; for VAT general taxpayer status, annual taxable sales exceeding RMB 5,000,000 (rolling 12 months) is the mandatory compulsory registration threshold, below which small-scale taxpayer treatment applies unless general VAT taxpayer status is voluntarily selected.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China requires near-real-time invoice clearance through the State Taxation Administration's national invoice control environment under the Golden Tax Phase IV system and the unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform (EISP). Registered taxpayers must issue fully digitalized electronic invoices (FDEI) with STA-issued digital certificates; each invoice is transmitted to STA at issuance, receives a nationally unique invoice number and statutory digital tax control seal, and is crosschecked against VAT return data, bank receipts, and customs records. High-volume sellers are expected to integrate with the EISP through government-approved APIs or certified tax-control software, and no unfiled offline VAT invoice may support input VAT credit or an export refund claim.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical goods exported from PRC customs territory may be zero-rated under the export goods VAT exemption, credit, and refund method once the goods are actually shipped out of China, the customs export declaration is released, the export sale is properly invoiced, and export proceeds are repatriated in accordance with SAFE foreign exchange rules. Qualifying offshore digital services and copyright/licensing-type transactions supplied to an overseas recipient may be zero-rated or VAT exempt if the service is consumed wholly outside China, the recipient is located outside China, and the contract, consideration, and delivery evidence demonstrate an offshore supply. The stock-photo and AI-generated visual asset marketplace must maintain the customer side, user location, delivery record, payment trail, and licensing terms to prove the cross-border nature of each zero-rated supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration (Customs Export Declaration) bearing the official export declaration number
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or combined transport document evidencing actual export from PRC customs territory
Commercial invoice and the export supply contract or digital order agreement with the overseas customer
Bank Foreign Exchange Collection Certificate or SAFE export proceeds settlement/foreign exchange repatriation record
For zero-rated digital services, supplementary delivery and consumption evidence such as server logs, user-country data, licensing agreements, and payment receipts from outside China
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, Customs, and SAFE jointly audit zero-rating claims by matching customs declarations, logistics confirmations, VAT invoice chains, corporate income tax filings, and bank foreign exchange receipts. If export zero-rating is approved without genuine customs exit, without valid FX repatriation within the statutory deadline, or with forged documentation or circular payments, the taxpayer must repay the refunded VAT plus daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05% of the unpaid tax, and is subject to an administrative penalty of between one and five times the tax involved; criminal liability for fraudulent export tax refund is pursued where the conduct meets the statutory threshold.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese yuan (CNY/RMB) is only partially convertible. Current account transactions, including trade in services and ordinary cross-border settlement, are broadly liberalised and may be effected through designated domestic banks after legitimate background verification. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity investment into the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, are heavily regulated by SAFE and require foreign-exchange registration, specified bank account structures, and genuine-transaction evidence. Foreign direct investment equity contributions may be remitted into a SAFE-registered capital account and subsequently settled to RMB for permitted uses, but the proceeds cannot be deployed for prohibited areas such as securities investment, real estate beyond the approved scope, or interbank lending. Profit and dividend remittance to the foreign shareholder is feasible after corporate income tax settlement, statutory reserve allocation, audited financial statements, and a board/shareholder dividend resolution; the remittance itself must pass through a domestic commercial bank with a completed tax payment certificate or withholding tax certificate and the correct SAFE service-trade or income-remittance purpose code. The JV must therefore distinguish carefully between current account flows, which are largely free after verification, and capital account flows, which are subject to quotas, registrations, and post-payment monitoring. Full offshore convertibility is not available; no unregulated fintech channel may substitute for the SAFE-approved banking channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current SAFE rules, export foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to a domestic bank account within the statutory time limit, normally 180 days from customs declaration, invoice date, or contractual payment due date unless SAFE has granted an extension for documented cause. The historical universal surrender requirement has been abolished; an exporter may retain eligible foreign exchange in its current-account FX settlement account or sell it to the bank for RMB, subject to SAFE authenticity verification and aggregated account limits. There is no fixed national mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts, but any amount exceeding the approved retention limit must be converted into RMB. The JV must supply the verifying bank with signed export contracts, customs declaration records, commercial invoices, receipts confirmation, logistics documentation, and the relevant balance-of-payments transaction records. Failure to repatriate within the required period or to provide genuine trade documentation will result in SAFE penalties and AML scrutiny.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Account for FDI Equity Injection and Basic Operational RMB Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Operating Account
FDI Capital Settlement Account and Trade Disbursement Account
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and RMB General Deposits Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Restricted / Auxiliary Only. Offshore digital EMIs such as Stripe and PayPal are not licensed as commercial banks or designated foreign-exchange banks in mainland China; they cannot operate as the primary cross-border settlement and clearing rail for a PRC-incorporated joint venture. PBOC and SAFE require all foreign-exchange receipts and payments for current and capital account transactions to be processed through designated domestic banks with underlying transaction verification and SAFE reporting. EMIs may be used only as supplementary customer-facing collection interfaces for digital stock-photo subscriptions and royalties, with funds ultimately settled into a domestic bank account in RMB and reconciled against platform merchant statements. Using an offshore EMI to route capital injections, profit distributions, or export-proceeds repatriation would violate SAFE regulations and cannot be recommended as a compliant treasury solution. Core liquidity and FX clearing must remain with tier-1 domestic commercial banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative of the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must physically appear at the domestic bank branch for the initial KYC interview, together with the company chop, original business license, completed articles of association, and a valid identity document. Authorised signatories must also be identified in a board resolution. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted by major Chinese banks for a newly formed JV; although powers of attorney executed abroad may be accepted after notarisation and apostille/legalisation by the Chinese consulate, the legal representative or an authorised officer with a valid notarised authorization must still attend the interview in person or, in limited exceptional cases, complete an identical videoconference interview approved by the bank's compliance unit. The bank will verify the physical office address and expect documentary proof of actual business premises, business plan, and the ultimate beneficial ownership of every shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity where a foreign holding company controls the JV through indirect layers and the bank cannot identify the underlying natural persons owning 25% or more of the equity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised register of members for every corporate shareholder, a step-by-step ownership diagram, certified copies of passports of all ultimate beneficial owners, apostilled/legalised beneficial-ownership declarations, corporate charters of each intermediate holding entity, board minutes approving the JV formation, source-of-wealth statements, and a signed undertaking confirming no undisclosed nominee or undisclosed principal exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The stated business scope involves AI-generated stock photography and licensing of digital visual assets, which may create red flags around intangible-asset valuation, royalty transfer pricing, and cross-border IP payments to foreign contributors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the fully executed copyright and content licensing agreements, a detailed intellectual-property flow chart, merchant platform agreements with Stripe and PayPal, sample sales invoices, historical subscriber or transaction records, a transfer-pricing documentation file demonstrating arm's-length royalty rates, PRC withholding-tax certificates for outbound payments, and a written commercial-substance narrative explaining the JV's role in curation, AI model licensing, hosting, and distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection into a newly incorporated JV with no operating income or tangible assets, creating a potential layer in a money-laundering or fraud scheme.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the approved feasibility study and business plan, board resolution approving the capital increase, notarised financial statements of the foreign investor for the last two fiscal years, bank statements evidencing legitimate source of funds, proof of taxation residence, shareholder loan agreements, a capital utilisation schedule tied to procurement, marketing, data infrastructure, AI model licensing, and employee compensation, and a commitment letter to provide post-disbursement usage reports and capital verification reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value card-not-present receipts through Stripe and PayPal for digital stock-photo downloads, which may trigger automated AML monitoring for micro-transaction structuring, chargebacks, or cross-border merchant-service mismatches.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the merchant account identifiers, transaction-level export files from both payment platforms, subscriber agreements, refund and dispute policies, detailed product-level metadata proving genuine photo-asset sales, monthly settlement statements showing net proceeds remitted to the domestic bank account, a data-privacy and fraud-prevention compliance policy, and periodic reconciliations aligning platform payouts with SAFE-verified trade-service declarations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must remit the equity investment capital via SWIFT MT103 with the correct SAFE foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign direct investment capital contributions (aligned with BOP code 622 for FDI capital injection) and must clearly reference the beneficiary as the joint venture's capital account at the designated domestic commercial bank. Prior to remittance, the JV must complete the SAFE FDI foreign-exchange registration and obtain the FX Registration Certificate or electronic registration record from the local SAFE or delegated bank. Upon receipt, the domestic bank will credit the capital account, verify the remittance narrative matches the registration, and record the capital settlement. The JV may then apply for RMB settlement of the foreign currency using the real-need mechanism, providing contracts, invoices, tax declarations, and a board-approved fund-use plan. A PRC-registered certified public accountant must thereafter issue a capital verification report confirming the subscribed capital has been actually paid. All documents must be retained for SAFE post-supervision and annual reporting; profit repatriation later will require an additional tax clearance and dividend remittance purpose code.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound disbursements to foreign photographers, AI model licensors, and content contributors, the JV should use SWIFT MT103 payments with the SAFE service-trade purpose code corresponding to royalties, licensing fees, or professional service fees. Each remittance must be supported by the underlying service agreement, invoices, tax withholding certificate, proof of tax payment, and a transaction authenticity statement submitted through the bank's electronic verification system. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not appropriate clearing rails for purely digital stock-photo asset purchases; those instruments should be reserved for physical goods procurement if the JV later acquires hardware, servers, or other tangible items. All outbound payments must be cleared through the domestic bank and reported to SAFE via the direct reporting system; funds cannot be paid from a fintech wallet without first being settled into the domestic bank account and passing normal current-account verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward contracts with a licensed PRC domestic bank, limited to the JV's genuine current-account or approved capital-account exposure
Cross-currency swaps between CNY and USD or EUR executed through a designated domestic bank under a SAFE-approved underlying trade, investment, or borrowing position

CNY/USD and CNY/EUR options with real trade background through a qualified domestic bank, subject to the JV's documented risk-management policy; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted as onshore hedging instruments for domestic PRC entities and may only be available to offshore counterparties outside SAFE supervision, so they are not a viable treasury hedge for this JV

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report Filing and Enterprise Information Annual Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from January 1 to June 30, covering the previous calendar year. Newly established entities must submit their first annual report by June 30 of the year following registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 results in the entity being listed in the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations. Continued non-filing for more than two consecutive years triggers inclusion in the List of Seriously Dishonest Enterprises, leading to public credit stigma, restricted market entry, strengthened supervision, and potential revocation of business license after three years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individual Income Tax Annual Reconciliation Filing for Employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between March 1 and June 30 for the preceding tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to RMB 2,000 per occurrence, late-payment surcharges of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax, tax enforcement measures, credit rating downgrades, and travel or consumption restrictions for responsible persons.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Final Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 following the end of each calendar tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of RMB 2,000 per return; late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on unpaid tax; repeated or serious violations may trigger tax authority inspection, asset seizure, bank account freezes, and tax credit rating downgrade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Stamp Duty Annual Declaration and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed quarterly or monthly depending on taxpayer classification; annual filing due by January 15 of the following year for taxpayers using the annual assessment method.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to RMB 2,000; late payment surcharges at 0.05% per day; liability orders, enforced collection, and tax credit downgrade.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Exchange Annual Reporting and SAFE Compliance Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For foreign-invested enterprises, annual joint reporting is typically required by June 30 each year through the Ministry of Commerce reporting system; direct SAFE annual verification may be required for entities engaged in cross-border payments.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warnings, fines up to RMB 300,000 for violation of foreign exchange registration rules, restrictions on cross-border profit repatriation, and downgrade in foreign exchange business compliance rating.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statistical Reporting Obligations to National Bureau of Statistics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Bureau of Statistics via local statistics bureaus
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reports for the preceding year are generally due between January 1 and May 31, depending on the reporting category assigned by the local statistics bureau.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to RMB 200,000 for refusal or delay in submitting statistical reports; repeated failure may trigger further administrative penalties, public credit records, and forced corrections under the Statistics Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Social Insurance and Housing Fund Annual Declaration Adjustment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Social Insurance Bureaus and Housing Provident Fund Management Centers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Typically each July for the following July-June contribution year, based on the previous calendar year average salary; local municipal notices govern exact dates.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears of social insurance premiums incur daily late fees of 0.05%; non-enrollment or under-declaration triggers rectification orders, fines from RMB 500 to RMB 10,000, and potential freezing of corporate bank accounts for enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is mandated for all enterprises under the Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises where any of the following applies: (a) the enterprise is a company limited by shares, a foreign-invested enterprise, a state-owned enterprise, or an enterprise applying the large-enterprise accounting standard; (b) the enterprise's annual operating revenue exceeds RMB 30 million (approximately USD 4.2 million); (c) total assets exceed RMB 40 million (approximately USD 5.6 million); (d) the enterprise has more than 50 employees; (e) the enterprise is required by its articles, joint venture contract, or shareholders' resolution to undergo an annual audit; or (f) the enterprise is involved in public interest activities, licensed financial operations, fundraising, or cross-border investment funds requiring audited financial statements. For small and micro enterprises eligible for the Simplified Accounting Standards, audit may be exempt unless lenders, tax authorities, or business partners require an audit report.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises, substantially converged with IFRS, for large and medium enterprises; Small Business Enterprise Accounting Standards for qualifying small firms; all foreign-invested enterprises must present financial statements prepared in RMB and in Chinese, and joint ventures typically follow ASBE with supplementary IFRS reporting for foreign parent company consolidation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: China does not maintain a public annual UBO confirmation form for ordinary domestic joint ventures; however, foreign-invested enterprises must annually report ultimate beneficial owner information through the Ministry of Commerce Foreign Investment Comprehensive Information Reporting System by June 30 each year. Additionally, any change of shareholders, registered capital, equity transfer, or beneficial ownership must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the change, and changes affecting foreign investors must be reported to MOFCOM/SAFE within 30 days for FDI registration and foreign exchange registration updates. A 30-day reporting window therefore applies both to annual information updates and to all material shareholding or control transfers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150 - USD 900 annually, depending on city tier and service provider; registered address in free trade zones or specialized foreign-invested enterprise service packages may range from USD 300 to USD 1,500
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - USD 3,500 for a small to medium-sized joint venture with standard stock photography/IP licensing transactions; USD 3,500 - USD 10,000 for entities requiring IFRS-basis audit reports for foreign parent consolidation or cross-border financing

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises may enjoy a reduced 15% corporate income tax rate; small low-profit enterprises may benefit from concessional rates on taxable income below statutory thresholds; eligible R&D expenses may be deducted at an additional 100%; certain encouraged regional or zone-based incentives may reduce the effective rate if the entity meets substance, industry, and location conditions. No general patent box regime exists for stock-photo or AI-generated content, but income from qualifying software or embedded copyright may be eligible for separate VAT and CIT policies where conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A) filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal and e-Login system, together with the Quarterly/Monthly Corporate Income Tax Prepayment Return; non-resident withholding at source is separately reported through the Non-Resident Enterprise Tax Withholding Return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement with quarterly prepayments; quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return and final tax payment must be completed by 31 May following the fiscal year-end; quarterly prepayments must be filed and paid by the 15th day of the month following each quarter; where dividends, interest, or royalties are paid to non-residents, the withholding agent must remit the withheld tax within 7 days after the obligation arises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from stock-photo licensing, AI-generated visual asset sales, subscription access, and platform commission fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue on a worldwide basis as a Chinese resident enterprise. For cross-border digital sales to non-resident customers, apply China source rules based on place of performance, payer residence, or royalty source principles; exclude VAT where separately shown; do not net intercompany settlements unless there is a documented arm's length transfer pricing policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including royalties or commissions paid to contributing photographers, content licensing fees, cloud server costs, and AI model hosting costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses that are ordinary, necessary, properly documented, and connected to taxable revenue. Cross-border royalty or service payments to non-resident affiliates must satisfy arm's length standards, beneficial ownership conditions, and withholding tax obligations; failure to substantiate may result in expense disallowance and transfer pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general and administrative expenses, including marketing, payment processing fees to Stripe and PayPal, and legal or accounting fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow bribes, fines, penalties, excessive entertainment expenses, and related-party management fees paid to non-resident affiliates without real services or economic substance. Cross-border payment processing fees should be allocated and documented based on commercial substance and should be reported in the related-party transaction schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit before financial items and non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The operating margin shown must be consistent with a benchmarked arm's length result. If the entity contracts with foreign related parties for distribution, licensing, or data services, the return must reflect a functional and risk profile that supports the reported margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income, including government grants, foreign exchange gains, and asset disposal gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable government grants must be included unless an express exemption applies; foreign exchange gains on intercompany receivables or payables must be recognized in accordance with PRC accounting standards and cannot be selectively recognized to reduce taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating expenses, including donations, asset impairments, and penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax penalties, unlawful payments, and fines are not deductible. Charitable donations are deductible only within statutory limits when made through eligible public welfare organizations; impairment losses on intercompany receivables must be supported by evidence of genuine credit terms and collection efforts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting total profit before tax and reconciliation to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare the tax reconciliation schedules to add back non-deductible expenses, adjust tax-exempt income, and reflect permanent and temporary differences. Complete the related-party transaction reporting schedules for tangible assets, intangible assets, services, and financing if any related-party transaction threshold is triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by the applicable corporate income tax rate, reduced by tax credits, prepayments, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate unless a lower preferential rate is approved; if the entity is a High and New Technology Enterprise, use 15%. When distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder, the entity as withholding agent must separately file the non-resident withholding return and deposit 10% WHT before remittance unless treaty relief has been approved.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return may attract a fine under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Law of up to RMB 2,000 for ordinary cases and up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases; late payment triggers a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. False reporting or fraudulent underpayment is penalized under Article 63 at 50% to 500% of the tax shortfall, with confiscation of illegal proceeds. Where tax evasion is criminal, Article 201 of the Criminal Law may impose imprisonment up to 3 years for a relatively large amount exceeding 10% of the tax payable, or 3 to 7 years where the amount is huge and exceeds 30% of the tax payable, plus fines; the legal representative and directly responsible managers may face criminal detention, asset freezing, exit restriction, and tax blacklisting.
